title: Halting Along a Deterministic Run
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine, with oracle, input bit string, and configuration guard $G$ fixed. Suppose that $T$ steps of the machine obtained by replacing every choice instruction by the fixed return value $ eta$ take configuration $a$ to $a'$. At every time $t<T$, suppose the configuration reached from $a$ satisfies $G$, and whenever it is live its current instruction in $A$ is deterministic. If the halting condition holds for $N$ steps from $a'$, then it holds for $T+N$ steps from $a$.
hypotheses_covered: The deterministic-part run for $T$ steps from $a$ reaches $a'$
At each time $t<T$, the run configuration satisfies $G$
At each time $t<T$, every live run configuration has a deterministic instruction
The halting condition holds for $N$ steps from $a'$
